claims.text: Laser surface cladding of a TiAl/TiC composite coating onto Ti-6Al-4V will increase surface hardness and wear resistance relative to the untreated alloy.
The starting material is an as-received structural titanium alloy such as Ti-6Al-4V.
Laser processing of a TiAl/TiC powder mixture will form an in-situ composite coating on the titanium alloy surface.
Cladding under ambient atmosphere can be parameterized to produce fine intermetallic phases and grain refinement.
The proposed improvement will hold in room-temperature reciprocating sliding wear at a controlled load such as 10 N.
The cladding layer will contain hard TiAl and TiC phases.
Laser cladding will refine the near-surface microstructure.
The cladding layer will possess compressive residual stresses.
Laser cladding of the TiAl/TiC mixture promotes the generation of hard, wear-resistant phases.
The intrinsic hardness and compressive stresses of the composite layer resist plastic deformation.
The composite layer suppresses abrasive and adhesive wear.
The coating could approximately double hardness or increase it by 60–70% over the substrate.
The cladded alloy will have a markedly lower wear rate than the untreated alloy.
The effect depends on obtaining an appropriate coating thickness and composition within typical laser-cladding process windows.
The magnitude of hardness and wear improvement will vary with cladding parameters and powder composition.
The expected relative hardness improvement lies in the range of 50–70%.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome allows an approximate doubling of hardness, equivalent to about a 100% increase, whereas the uncertainty field bounds the expected improvement at 50–70%.
